content: Magnesium oxide is a medication that serves multiple purposes. Magnesium is an essential element required for the normal functioning of the body. Magnesium oxide can be used as an antacid to alleviate symptoms such as heartburn, sour stomach, or acid indigestion. It may also be used as a laxative for short-term purposes, such as rapid bowel evacuation before surgery. However, it is not intended for repeated or long-term use. Additionally, magnesium oxide can act as a dietary supplement for individuals whose dietary intake of magnesium is insufficient. This medication is available over the counter, but it may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Magnesium oxide is available in tablet and capsule forms, which are taken orally. The dosage frequency typically ranges from one to four times daily, depending on the brand and the condition being treated. It is crucial to follow the instructions provided on the packaging or prescription label carefully. If you have any doubts, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take magnesium oxide exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. When using magnesium oxide as a laxative, consume it with a full glass (8 ounces) of cold water or fruit juice. Avoid taking a dose late in the day on an empty stomach. Do not use magnesium oxide as an antacid for more than two weeks or as a laxative for more than one week unless directed by your doctor. Before starting magnesium oxide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to magnesium oxide, other antacids or laxatives, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially if they include other antacids or laxatives, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), aspirin, diuretics, ulcer medications, or vitamins. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking magnesium oxide, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are following a low-salt, low-sugar, or any other special diet. If you are taking magnesium oxide on a regular schedule and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Magnesium oxide may cause side effects. To minimize an unpleasant taste, take the tablet with citrus fruit juice or a carbonated citrus drink. Minor side effects may include cramping and diarrhea. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention and may include rash or hives, itching, dizziness or lightheadedness, mood or mental changes, unusual tiredness, weakness, upset stomach, or vomiting. If you experience a severe side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store magnesium oxide in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Do not share this medication with others. Magnesium oxide is sold under various brand names, including Mag-Ox®, Maox®, and Uro-Mag®.
